title: D. Retaliation
statement:
Yousef wants to explode an array a_1, a_2, …, a_n. An array gets exploded when all of its elements become equal to zero.

In one operation, Yousef can do exactly one of the following:

Your task is to help Yousef determine if it is possible to explode the array using any number of operations.

The first line of the input contains an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^4) — the number of test cases.

The first line of each test case contains an integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5) — the size of the array.

The second line of each test case contains n integers a_1, a_2, …, a_n (1 ≤ a_i ≤ 10^9) — the elements of the array.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n over all test cases doesn't exceed 2·10^5.

For each test case, print "YES" if Yousef can explode the array, otherwise output "NO".

You can output the answer in any case (upper or lower). For example, the strings "yEs", "yes", "Yes", and "YES" will be recognized as positive responses.

In the second test case, we can do the following:

In the first, third, fourth, and sixth test cases, it can be proven that it is impossible to make all elements equal to zero using any number of operations.

Input:
```
643 6 6 3521 18 15 12 9102 6 10 2 5 5 1 2 4 10710 2 16 12 8 20 4252 101210 2
```

Output:
```
NO
YES
NO
NO
YES
NO
```
